title: Saw-Pit
summary: SAW'-PIT, noun A pit over which timber is sawed by two men, one standing below the timber and the other above. SAW'-WORT, noun A plant of the genus Serratula, so named from its serrated leaves. SAW'-W

inlines.v: SAW'-PIT, noun A pit over which timber is sawed by two men, one standing below the timber and the other above. SAW'-WORT, noun A plant of the genus Serratula, so named from its serrated leaves. SAW'-WREST, noun An instrument used to wrest or turn the teeth of saws a little outwards, that they may make a kerf somewhat wider than the thickness of the blade.
